overview: Coupang is South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, built around its proprietary end-to-end "Rocket Delivery" logistics network that offers free next-day (often same-day) delivery to the vast majority of Korean households. Founded by Bom Kim and listed on the NYSE (dual-class shares, Class A/B) since March 2021, Coupang combines first-party retail, a third-party marketplace, advertising, and the Rocket WOW membership program with a portfolio of "Developing Offerings" spanning food delivery (Eats), streaming (Play), fintech, Taiwan expansion, and global luxury fashion via its January 2024 acquisition of Farfetch. The company is now formally headquartered in Seattle, Washington but generates the substantial majority of revenue from Korea.

business_model.summary: Coupang earns most of its revenue from first-party (1P) product sales to Korean consumers, supplemented by third-party marketplace commissions, fulfillment/logistics fees, advertising, and the paid Rocket WOW subscription (~$4-5/month) that bundles free delivery, discounts, Play streaming, and (contested) Eats benefits. Product Commerce is high-volume/low-margin retail; Developing Offerings (Farfetch, Taiwan, Eats, Play, fintech) are earlier-stage, faster-growing, and currently loss-making, functioning as reinvestment vehicles for future profit pools.

revenue_streams.name: Developing Offerings (Farfetch, Taiwan, Eats, Play, fintech)

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market consumer, with a B2B/SME third-party merchant marketplace layer and a luxury B2C segment via Farfetch
business_model.geographic_mix: Korea is the core market (~95%+ of revenue); Developing Offerings add Taiwan retail and Farfetch's globally-distributed luxury customer base (Europe, US, Asia)

competitive_position.market_position: Co-leader (roughly neck-and-neck with Naver Shopping) in Korean e-commerce with an estimated ~24-25% of e-commerce GMV/revenue and higher share of online retail traffic/engagement; clear leader in same-day/next-day fulfillment logistics

moat_factors.description: Vertically integrated fulfillment centers, delivery fleet, and last-mile 'Coupang Man' couriers positioned within roughly 7 miles of ~70% of the Korean population enable free next-day (and often same-day/dawn) delivery that is very costly for competitors to replicate
High order density supports lower per-unit fulfillment cost, funding continued price competitiveness and reinvestment
Subscription bundles delivery, discounts, Play and (contested) Eats benefits, raising switching costs and driving purchase frequency
Strong reputation for reliability and speed in Korea, though damaged by the late-2025 data breach
Large first-party transaction dataset supports recommendation, inventory, and advertising optimization

weaknesses: Structurally thin retail margins versus asset-light marketplace competitors (Naver, AliExpress)
Heavy geographic concentration in a single, slow-growing, demographically shrinking market (Korea)
Developing Offerings (Taiwan, Farfetch, Eats) remain unprofitable and dilute consolidated margins
Vulnerable to low-price Chinese cross-border platforms (AliExpress, Temu) that undercut on price without Coupang's logistics cost base
Reputational and regulatory overhang from the November 2025 data breach

growth_drivers: WOW membership growth and monetization (higher spend per member, cross-sell into Play/Eats)
Advertising revenue scaling off the growing first-party retail base
Taiwan Rocket Delivery expansion replicating the Korean logistics playbook in a new geography
Farfetch turnaround/integration into Coupang's logistics and membership ecosystem, targeting luxury e-commerce growth
Coupang Eats and Coupang Play expansion, plus new Rocket Now food delivery in Japan
Fulfillment-as-a-service / FLC (Fulfillment and Logistics by Coupang) for third-party merchants
Continued automation and technology investment to expand Product Commerce margins
Capital return: $1B share repurchase program (May 2025), increased by an additional $1B in May 2026

business.risk: Intensifying competition from Chinese cross-border platforms
business.description: AliExpress and Temu are growing rapidly in Korea with aggressive pricing, pressuring Coupang's value proposition and potentially its take rate

business.risk: Post-breach customer trust and engagement erosion
business.description: Q1 2026 Product Commerce Active Customer growth slowed materially due to the Incident; management says ~80% of lost WOW memberships were recovered by April 2026, but full restoration is not yet confirmed

business.risk: Persistently thin/negative margins in Developing Offerings
business.description: Developing Offerings adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $(995)M in FY2025 from $(631)M in FY2024, and to $(329)M in Q1 2026 alone, as Farfetch, Taiwan, and Eats scale
Cost of sales runs ~70%+ of revenue; Product Commerce cost of sales ratio rose further in Q1 2026 due to breach-related compensation costs

financial.description: Nearly all operating revenue and costs are in Korean won while Coupang reports in USD; FX moves create reported-vs-constant-currency divergence (e.g., FX was a ~1% revenue headwind in Q1 2026)
Drew $750M on its revolving credit facility plus ~$928M under other credit facilities in Q1 2026 for general operating purposes, partly to fund breach-related costs and buybacks
TTM free cash flow fell to $301M (from $1,025M a year earlier) as of Q1 2026, and quarterly FCF was negative $(110)M, reflecting breach costs and Developing Offerings investment

regulatory.risk: KFTC search-ranking manipulation fine and criminal referral
regulatory.description: KFTC found Coupang Corp.'s product-ranking disclosures violated Korean law, imposed a ~$121M administrative fine (accrued Q2 2024, paid in installments through June 2026) and referred the matter for criminal prosecution; Coupang is appealing both the administrative fine/corrective orders and a related criminal indictment (hearings ongoing through mid-2026)

regulatory.risk: PIPC data breach fine and government scrutiny
regulatory.description: Following the November 2025 breach affecting ~33.7-37.5 million user records, Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission imposed a record fine of roughly 624.6 billion won (~$409-455 million, per press reports) in mid-2026, plus separate penalties for unlawful tracking of ~11.2 million users; multiple government agencies (PIPC, KISA, National Police Agency, prosecutors) are investigating, and criminal complaints have been filed against current/former executives and employees

regulatory.risk: KFTC investigation into WOW/Eats benefit bundling
regulatory.description: KFTC examiner's report (Oct 2025) argues bundling Eats benefits with WOW membership is impermissible under the Fair Trade Act; if upheld, Coupang could be forced to unbundle Eats and price it separately, denting membership value proposition

IPO-related securities class action was dismissed (Sept 2025, plaintiffs appealing) but new securities class actions and derivative suits were filed in Jan-Mar 2026 specifically tied to the data breach and alleged misleading disclosures
National Tax Service commenced an audit of 2021-2025 income tax and VAT filings in December 2025, outcome still open

macro.description: Long-term structural headwind to domestic e-commerce TAM growth given world-leading low birth rates and a contracting working-age population
Discretionary retail categories (including Farfetch luxury) are sensitive to Korean and global consumer confidence and disposable income
Broader US-China-Korea trade dynamics and tariff policy could affect cross-border sourcing costs and competitive dynamics with Chinese platforms

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Korean e-commerce penetration is already high and growth is moderating into the high-single/low-double digits, with growth increasingly driven by mix shift (fresh grocery, fashion/luxury, advertising) rather than new-shopper acquisition; Taiwan represents a earlier-stage, higher-growth adjacent market
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - grocery/staples portion of Product Commerce is fairly defensive, but discretionary categories (electronics, fashion, Farfetch luxury) are more cyclical and sensitive to consumer confidence
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct exposure (modest short-term borrowings/revolver draws), moderate indirect sensitivity via Korean consumer spending and Farfetch's debt-financed balance sheet
key_input_costs: Labor/fulfillment center staffing costs in Korea
Real estate/lease costs for fulfillment centers

recent_developments.event: Coupang became aware of a data incident involving unauthorized access to customer accounts by a former employee, exposing personal data (excluding payment info/passwords) of an estimated 33.7-37.5 million users, among the largest breaches in Korean corporate history

CEO Park Dae-jun resigned in the wake of the breach; Harold Rogers named interim CEO. Coupang announced a customer compensation program issuing ~$1.2 billion of vouchers to affected customers, redeemed primarily in Q1 2026 and concluding mid-April 2026

Multiple new securities class actions (Lee and Park v. Coupang) and stockholder derivative suits (Warga v. Bom Kim, Wilson v. Coupang) filed in US federal courts alleging misleading statements and governance failures related to the data incident

Q4/FY2025 results: full-year revenue grew 14% to $34.5B (18% constant currency), gross profit +15% to $10.1B (29.4% margin), net income improved to $214M from $66M in FY2024; Developing Offerings revenue (Farfetch + Taiwan-driven) more than quadrupled versus prior levels but Developing Offerings adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $(995)M
May 2026: Board authorized an additional $1 billion increase to the stock repurchase program (on top of the May 2025 $1B authorization); ~$391M of shares repurchased in Q1 2026 alone

Q1 2026 results: revenue +8% YoY to $8.5B, but company swung to an operating loss of $(242)M and net loss of $(266)M (adjusted EBITDA fell 92% to $29M) as data-breach remediation and compensation costs hit margins; management guided Q2 2026 constant-currency revenue growth of 9-10% with consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin still contracting 300-400bps YoY, while reporting ~80% of lost WOW memberships recovered by April 2026 and churn reverting toward historical norms

Korea's PIPC levied a record fine of roughly 624.6 billion won (~$409-455 million per various reports) against Coupang for the data breach and separately for unlawful collection of online activity data from ~11.2 million users without consent; KFTC search-ranking case administrative litigation and criminal trial proceedings continued with hearings through mid-2026

SoftBank continued reducing its Coupang stake, selling roughly $1.6-1.7 billion (2.3 trillion won) of shares across 2025, cutting its position from over 32% (2021) to roughly 17%, reportedly to fund AI-related investments elsewhere in its portfolio

items.notes: Guidance for Q2 came in ahead of prior Street expectations per Morgan Stanley commentary, reflecting faster-than-expected recovery in Korea engagement post-breach

Primarily attributed to temporary factors tied to the November 2025 data incident (remediation costs, compensation program tail, elevated marketing/retention spend) plus continued Developing Offerings investment
Management characterized churn as reverting to historical levels; full recovery trajectory not yet quantified for remainder of FY2026

guidance.management_commentary: Management framed Q1 2026 as reflecting the peak financial impact of the data incident (voucher redemption concentrated in Q1, concluding mid-April 2026) and pointed to rapid restoration of customer engagement and WOW membership as evidence the franchise is recovering. Management continues to frame Developing Offerings (Farfetch, Taiwan, Eats) losses as investment in future profit pools rather than structural, while emphasizing capital discipline via the expanded buyback authorization.

bull_case: Dominant, hard-to-replicate logistics infrastructure gives Coupang a durable cost/speed advantage in Korean e-commerce that is difficult for asset-light rivals (Naver) or low-price entrants (AliExpress, Temu) to match

Early signs the data-breach-driven customer and membership attrition are proving temporary, with ~80% of lost WOW members recovered within months and Q2 2026 revenue growth guidance raised versus expectations

Farfetch and Taiwan are scaling rapidly (Developing Offerings revenue up sharply) and could become meaningful profit contributors once they reach the density Coupang achieved in Korean Product Commerce
Growing, high-margin advertising and WOW membership subscription revenue provide a path to structural margin expansion even within a low-margin retail base

Management is returning capital via an expanded $2B cumulative buyback authorization while the stock trades near multi-year lows (~55% off its 52-week high), which bulls view as a valuation opportunity if the breach overhang fades
bear_case: The November 2025 data breach caused a CEO resignation, a record ~$409-455M PIPC fine, a $1.2B customer compensation program, and multiple new securities/derivative lawsuits — cumulative direct and reputational costs could keep pressuring margins and growth well beyond Q1-Q2 2026

Structural exposure to a single, demographically shrinking market (Korea) limits the long-term total addressable market, while Chinese cross-border platforms (AliExpress, Temu) are taking share on price

Developing Offerings (Farfetch, Taiwan, Eats, Play) remain deeply unprofitable with widening losses ($(995)M FY2025 adjusted EBITDA loss), and there is no guarantee they achieve Korea-level unit economics

Ongoing, unresolved KFTC search-ranking manipulation case (administrative appeal plus criminal trial) and the separate WOW/Eats bundling investigation could result in additional fines, forced product changes (unbundling Eats), and prolonged reputational damage with Korean regulators

Free cash flow has deteriorated sharply (TTM FCF down to $301M from $1,025M a year prior) alongside rising short-term borrowings, reducing financial flexibility just as buyback commitments and regulatory costs increase
